    Sources and adaptation notes¶

    The course adapts practical habits from university laboratories and applies them to a supervised Quiver build. Local procedures and the actual equipment manuals determine authorisation and operating limits.

    Daily laboratory practice¶

    S1 Maryland Robotics Drone Lab — Rules and safety. Used for assigned storage, authorised tools and returning equipment. Its local flight thresholds, emergency contacts and instructions to move burning equipment are not adopted.

    S2 Fresno State — Electronics laboratory safety, operating guidelines 14 to 16. Used for component trays, lead racks, keeping probes with instruments and bench reset. Its local network rules are not UNILAG rules.

    S3 Penn State Behrend — Laboratory and shop procedures. Used for documented equipment training, proper return and damaged-item reporting. Local access rules and penalties are not transferred.

    S4 Queen Mary University of London — Research labs and drones. Used for supervised charging, inspection and protected storage. UK law references and emergency numbers are not Nigerian requirements.

    S5 NUbots — Lab induction checklist, battery items 1.1 to 1.6 and signatures. It records instruction and acknowledgement. Our observed student demonstrations are an added Quiver course design choice. Its software ownership agreement is not adopted.

    Equipment and education¶

    S6 NIOSH — Approaches to safe 3D printing. Emissions and controls for makerspaces and schools.

    S7 ArduPilot — SITL documentation and motor setup safety. Verify the exact hardware and software before applying instructions.

    S8 UNILAG — Student centred learning guideline and university policies.

    S9 NUC — Engineering CCMAS. Programme context; the department determines any credit mapping.

    S10 NCAA — Part 21 RPAS. Check current requirements before real flight operations.

    Design and provenance¶

    Use short procedures, nearby diagrams, worked examples and repeated practice. CDC information chunking and IES instructional guidance inform this approach. They do not prescribe this course's assessment threshold.

    Version 5.1 prepared 25 October 2026. The aircraft photo is an unaltered project asset; diagrams are conceptual teaching aids. Project technical references are listed on the next page.
